intro: Portugal’s sunny south coast: golden cliffs and sea caves, fishing towns, golf and lively summer nights.
areas: Ponta da Piedade cliffs, beaches and a historic old town.
Busy resort nightlife, Benagil caves and family beaches.
The regional capital, Ria Formosa lagoon and Tavira.
Vilamoura, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo for golf and marinas.
sights: Famous sea cave, seen by boat or kayak tour (landing on the beach is restricted).
Rock arches and grottoes near Lagos.
Protected lagoon with boat trips to barrier islands.
Europe’s south-western tip and its fortress.
Historic town with a red sandstone castle.
eat: Seafood stew cooked in a copper pan.
Local fruit brandy from the hills.
night: Avenida Sá Carneiro bars and clubs, busiest in summer.
arrive: Faro Airport serves the whole region; buses and taxis link it to the resorts. Trains run along the coast from Lagos to Vila Real de Santo António, with connections to Lisbon.
around: Regional trains and Vamus buses connect the towns; a hire car is easiest for beaches and villages.
pass: Vamus Algarve and regional rail tickets are bought per journey; check current passes.
when: May–June and September–October for warm seas and fewer crowds; July–August is peak season.
tip: Book cave boat trips early in the day when the sea is usually calmer.

intro: Portugal’s sunlit capital of seven hills, vintage trams, fado and miradouros above the Tagus.
areas: Lisbon’s oldest quarter, with fado houses and the castle.
Monuments, museums and the famous custard tarts.
sights: Art, design and a creative quarter by the river.
Fairy-tale palaces about 40 minutes by train.
eat: Food hall in Mercado da Ribeira.
Cherry liqueur served in small shots.
arrive: Lisbon Airport (Humberto Delgado) is linked by Metro (red line) and taxis. Santa Apolónia and Oriente stations have trains to Porto and the Algarve.
around: Metro, trams, buses, funiculars and ferries; hills make walking tough, so use trams and lifts.
pass: Navegante card with zapping credit or a 24-hour ticket; the Lisboa Card adds museum entries.
when: March–June and September–October; June brings the Santo António festivals.
tip: Tram 28 gets crowded and is a pickpocket hotspot; ride early or walk the route.

intro: Porto tumbles down to the Douro in a cascade of tiled houses, port lodges and bridges.
areas: Avenida dos Aliados, São Bento station and Rua de Santa Catarina.
Port wine cellars across the river.
Seafront promenade where the river meets the Atlantic.
sights: Hall lined with azulejo tile panels.
Vineyard day trips by train, boat or car.
eat: Porto’s famous meat-and-cheese sandwich with sauce.
arrive: Porto Airport is on the Metro (purple line). Campanhã and São Bento stations have trains to Lisbon and the Douro.
around: Metro, buses, historic trams and the Guindais funicular.
pass: Andante card for Metro and buses; the Porto Card adds museum discounts.
when: April–June and September–October; São João festival on 23–24 June.
tip: Watch the sunset from the Jardim do Morro above the bridge.

intro: A subtropical Atlantic island of levada walks, cliffs, flowers and Funchal’s lively harbour.
areas: Capital with the old town, markets and gardens.
Hilltop gardens and the toboggan ride down.
Porto Moniz pools and dramatic cliffs.
sights: Skywalk over one of Europe’s highest sea cliffs.
eat: Honey and lemon cane-spirit poncha, or fortified wine.
night: Bars along Rua de Santa Maria.
One of the world’s biggest displays.
arrive: Madeira Airport (Cristiano Ronaldo) is linked to Funchal by Aerobus and taxi.
around: Buses link towns; a hire car or tour helps for walks. Roads are steep and winding.
pass: Buy bus tickets per journey or a multi-trip card; check current options.
when: Year-round mild climate; spring for flowers; New Year for fireworks.
tip: Check official trail status before levada walks, as some close after bad weather.

intro: The Algarve’s liveliest resort: cliff-backed beaches, a whitewashed old town and a famous nightlife strip.
areas: Whitewashed streets above Praia dos Pescadores.
sights: Boat trips leave from nearby beaches.
eat: Guia is known for its chicken.
Seafood stew cooked in a copper pan.
arrive: Faro Airport is about 35–40 minutes by road. Albufeira-Ferreiras station is a few kilometres inland.
around: Local buses and taxis; the old town is walkable but hilly.
pass: Buy local bus tickets per journey; check current options.
when: May–October; July–August is busiest.
tip: Take the escalator down from the clifftop to Praia dos Pescadores.

intro: Portugal’s historic university city, with a World Heritage campus above the Mondego and fado sung by students.
areas: Lower town with shopping streets and cafés.
Across the river, with the old convent.
sights: World Heritage site with the Joanina Library.
night: Sung by men in student capes.
arrive: Coimbra-B station has trains to Lisbon and Porto. Porto and Lisbon airports are about 1–2 hours away.
around: Walk (steep); SMTUC buses.
pass: SMTUC tickets per journey; check current options.
when: Spring and autumn; May for student festivities.
tip: Book Joanina Library tickets for a timed slot.

intro: Portugal’s religious capital, with baroque churches, the Bom Jesus staircase and a youthful buzz.
areas: World Heritage sanctuary above the city.
sights: Medieval birthplace of Portugal, close by.
arrive: Porto Airport is about 45 minutes by road (airport buses run). Braga station has trains to Porto.
around: Walkable centre; TUB buses to Bom Jesus.
pass: TUB tickets per journey; check current options.
when: Spring to autumn; Holy Week and São João (June).
tip: Take the water-powered funicular up to Bom Jesus and walk down the stairs.

intro: Gaudí, beaches and late nights: Barcelona mixes Gothic lanes, modernista icons and a famous food scene.
areas: Medieval lanes, the cathedral and the Picasso Museum.
Gaudí’s Casa Batlló and La Pedrera on grid streets.
Beach, seafood and the seafront promenade.
sights: Modernista houses on Passeig de Gràcia.
eat: Bombas, patatas bravas and pan con tomate.
arrive: Barcelona-El Prat Airport is linked by Aerobús, train (R2 Nord) and Metro L9 Sud. Sants station has high-speed trains to Madrid and France.
around: Metro, buses and trams; the centre is walkable.
pass: T-casual (10 trips) or Hola Barcelona travel cards; check current zones and fares.
when: May–June and September–October; August is hot and busy.
tip: Keep valuables zipped away on La Rambla and the Metro.

intro: Spain’s energetic capital of grand boulevards, world-class art and dinners that start late and end later.
areas: Puerta del Sol, Plaza Mayor and the Royal Palace.
Prado, Thyssen and Reina Sofía museums.
Bars, vintage shops and LGBTQ+ nightlife.
Tapas bars and the Sunday Rastro market.
sights: One of Europe’s largest royal palaces.
Lake, rowing boats and the Crystal Palace.
arrive: Madrid-Barajas Airport is linked by Metro (line 8), Cercanías trains and the Airport Express bus. Atocha and Chamartín have high-speed trains.
around: Metro is extensive and easy; buses and Cercanías trains too.
pass: Tourist Travel Pass (1–7 days) or a Multi card with 10-trip tickets; check current fares.
when: April–June and September–October; summer is very hot.
tip: Museums have free entry at set times; check each museum’s schedule.

intro: Andalusia’s passionate capital of flamenco, orange trees, a vast cathedral and Moorish palaces.
areas: Old Jewish quarter of lanes near the cathedral.
Across the river; ceramics, flamenco and tapas.
sights: Royal palace with Mudéjar halls and gardens.
One of the world’s largest Gothic cathedrals.
Grand pavilion in María Luisa Park.
Wooden canopy with a rooftop walkway.
eat: Salmorejo, espinacas con garbanzos and fried fish.
night: Shows and peñas, especially in Triana.
arrive: Seville Airport is linked by bus. Santa Justa station has high-speed trains to Madrid.
around: Walk; Metro, trams and buses for longer trips. Rent a bike on the cycle lanes.
pass: Tussam multi-trip card for buses; check current options.
when: March–May (Semana Santa and the April Fair) and October–November; summer is extremely hot.
tip: Book Alcázar tickets ahead; visit early in the morning.

intro: Picasso’s birthplace, with a Moorish fortress, a buzzing old town and beaches minutes from the centre.
areas: Calle Larios, the cathedral and Plaza de la Merced.
sights: Works by the city’s most famous son.
eat: Sardines grilled on skewers on the beach.
arrive: Málaga Airport is linked by Cercanías train (C1) and buses. María Zambrano station has high-speed trains to Madrid.
around: Walk; Metro and EMT buses cover the city; trains along the coast.
pass: EMT multi-trip cards; Cercanías tickets per journey.
when: April–June and September–November.
tip: Many museums offer free entry on Sunday afternoons; check each.

intro: World-famous club island with a World Heritage old town, hidden coves and spectacular sunsets.
areas: Dalt Vila, the port and the marina.
sights: Day trips by ferry to its beaches.
night: Big-name clubs in Sant Antoni and Playa d’en Bossa.
Café del Mar area in Sant Antoni.
arrive: Ibiza Airport is linked by bus and taxi. Ferries sail to Formentera, Denia, Valencia, Barcelona and Palma.
around: Buses connect towns; a hire car or scooter helps for coves. Taxis can be scarce in peak summer.
pass: Buy bus tickets on board or by app; check current options.
when: Late May–early October for clubs; spring and autumn for quieter days.
tip: Book club tickets online, and plan taxis or night buses home in advance.

intro: The largest Canary Island: Spain’s highest peak, year-round sunshine, whale watching and lively resorts.
areas: Northern town with gardens and pools.
Capital and World Heritage old town.
sights: Spain’s highest peak; cable car and trails.
Boat trips from the south-west coast.
eat: Rustic family eateries in the north.
night: Bars and clubs in the south.
Bars along the Costa Adeje beaches.
arrive: Tenerife South Airport serves the resorts; Tenerife North serves Santa Cruz and La Laguna. Buses and taxis link both.
around: TITSA buses cover the island; a tram runs in Santa Cruz–La Laguna. A hire car helps for Teide.
pass: Ten+ travel cards on TITSA buses; check current fares.
when: Year-round; winter is warm and popular.
tip: Book Teide cable car and summit permits in advance.

intro: The largest Balearic island: Palma’s Gothic cathedral, mountain villages and turquoise coves.
areas: Cathedral, old town and the seafront.
World Heritage mountains with Sóller and Deià.
Coves and the Caves of Drach.
arrive: Palma de Mallorca Airport is linked by bus to Palma. Ferries sail to Barcelona, Valencia and the other islands.
around: TIB buses island-wide; EMT buses in Palma. A hire car helps for the mountains.
pass: Intercard and TIB tickets; check current options.
when: May–June and September–October.
tip: Drive the Formentor road early; access is restricted at peak times.

intro: The home of paella, with futuristic architecture, a riverbed park and city beaches.
areas: Old town with the cathedral and Central Market.
night: Bars and clubs in a trendy district.
arrive: Valencia Airport is on the Metro (lines 3 and 5). Joaquín Sorolla station has high-speed trains to Madrid.
around: Metro, trams and EMT buses; Valenbisi bikes along the Turia.
pass: SUMA card or Valencia Tourist Card; check current options.
when: April–June and September–October; March for Las Fallas.
tip: Book a paella lunch near the beach or in El Palmar by the Albufera.

intro: A Basque city transformed by the Guggenheim, with a pintxos-packed old town and green hills.
areas: Seven Streets of the old town.
sights: World Heritage transporter bridge at Portugalete.
eat: Bar snacks, especially in Plaza Nueva.
arrive: Bilbao Airport is linked by Bizkaibus to the centre. Trains and buses link to San Sebastián and Madrid.
around: Metro Bilbao, trams and buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Barik card for Metro, tram and buses; check current options.
when: May–October; August for Aste Nagusia.
tip: Pintxos are paid as you go; ask for the bill at the end.

intro: Moorish Granada: the Alhambra, the Albaicín’s white lanes and tapas served free with your drink.
sights: Famous sunset view of the Alhambra.
eat: Many bars serve a tapa with each drink.
Street of tapas bars near the town hall.
Sweet pastries from nearby Santa Fe.
arrive: Federico García Lorca Granada Airport is linked by bus. Granada station has trains to Madrid and Málaga; Málaga Airport is about 90 minutes away.
around: Walk; minibuses climb the Albaicín and Alhambra.
pass: Credibus card for city buses; check current options.
when: Spring and autumn; Sierra Nevada skiing in winter.
tip: Alhambra tickets sell out; book weeks ahead for a Nasrid Palaces time slot.

intro: A sunny Costa Blanca city with a palm-lined promenade, a hilltop castle and a beach in town.
areas: Lanes, bars and Santa María Basilica.
Long sandy beach north of the city.
night: Bars and clubs in the old town.
arrive: Alicante-Elche Airport is linked by bus. Alicante station has high-speed trains to Madrid.
around: TRAM Alicante and buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: Móbilis card for tram and bus; check current options.
when: Year-round; May–June and September–October are ideal.
tip: Take the lift inside the mountain up to the castle.

intro: Skyscrapers, two long beaches and round-the-clock entertainment on the Costa Blanca.
areas: Balcón del Mediterráneo and tapas streets.
eat: Tapas bars in the old town.
night: Bars and clubs near Levante beach.
arrive: Alicante Airport is about 45 minutes away by bus or transfer. TRAM line 1 runs along the coast.
around: TRAM Alicante and local buses; walkable seafront.
pass: Móbilis card for the tram; check current options.
when: Year-round; spring and autumn are ideal.
tip: Watch the sunset from Poniente beach’s promenade.

intro: Costa del Sol glamour: a whitewashed old town, the Golden Mile and Puerto Banús.
areas: Plaza de los Naranjos and flower-filled streets.
sights: Orange-tree square in the old town.
Dalí sculptures on the way to the beach.
Clifftop town about an hour inland.
night: Bars and clubs at the marina.
arrive: Málaga Airport is about 45 minutes away by bus or transfer.
around: Avanza buses along the coast; taxis.
pass: Buy bus tickets per journey; check current options.
when: April–June and September–October.
tip: Puerto Banús prices are high; old-town restaurants are better value.

intro: A ‘miniature continent’ of dunes, mountains and beaches, with lively Las Palmas.
areas: Capital with Las Canteras beach and Vegueta.
sights: City beach with a natural reef.
night: LGBTQ+ nightlife in Playa del Inglés.
Bars and clubs near Las Canteras.
arrive: Gran Canaria Airport is linked by Global buses to Las Palmas and the south.
around: Global intercity buses; a hire car helps for the mountains.
pass: Bono cards on Global buses; check current options.
when: Year-round sun.
tip: Hike to Roque Nublo early to avoid clouds and crowds.

intro: A volcanic island of black lava fields, César Manrique art and golden beaches.
areas: Main resort with a long beach.
eat: In El Golfo and harbour towns.
night: Bars and clubs along the Avenida.
arrive: César Manrique-Lanzarote Airport is linked by bus and taxi to the resorts.
around: Arrecife Bus routes; a hire car is best for sights.
pass: Buy bus tickets per journey or a bono; check current options.
when: Year-round sun; can be windy.
tip: Combine Manrique sites with a discounted multi-centre ticket (check current options).

intro: A Basque seaside city famous for pintxos, Michelin stars and La Concha bay.
areas: Old town packed with pintxos bars.
Surf beach and a younger vibe.
sights: One of Europe’s best city beaches.
Castle walk above the old town.
arrive: San Sebastián Airport (Hondarribia) has limited flights; Bilbao and Biarritz airports are about an hour away.
around: Walk; Dbus buses and Euskotren trains.
pass: Mugi card for buses and trains; check current options.
when: June–September; January for the Tamborrada drum festival.
tip: Pintxos culture: a couple per bar, then move on.
